answer: One concrete mechanism: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because kernel only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice thread is enforced by the ledger itself: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any echo approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
